plan: Given my private value of $28, I should bid slightly below my value to maximize profit while still having a good chance of winning. Bidding exactly at my value or slightly below ensures I don't overpay if I win. Since all bidders are rational and values are uniformly distributed, bidding slightly below $28 can deter others who value it less, while still being competitive against those with similar or higher values. A bid of $27.9 balances the risk of losing with the potential profit margin.

Given my private value of $16, I will bid slightly below my value to maximize profit while still having a good chance to win. A rational strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of other bidders, around $10, since values are uniformly distributed. I will bid $15.9, just under my value, to ensure profit if I win. This bid is high enough to outbid most rational opponents, but low enough to ensure a profit margin.

Given my value of $19, I should bid slightly below my value to maximize profit while still having a high chance of winning. A rational bidder bids slightly above their value to avoid losing, but not too much to ensure profit. Bidding $18.9 maximizes my potential profit ($19 - $18.9) while still having a high probability of winning against rational bidders who will bid close to or slightly above their values.
